text:
Asha: Heads-up: debugging sampled requests is getting painful. we lose the link between sampled logs and the original fields that triggered bugs. proposal: compute a tenant-scoped deterministic id for sensitive fields so sampled traces can be joined without exposing raw PII.
Ben: Do you mean a salted hash? how is this different from the hashing RFC we already have?
Asha: similar but with explicit replay UX in mind. key differences: per-tenant KMS key for HMAC (no global salt), explicit field-level id stored alongside redacted value, and surrogate generation for safe replay.
Rory: Surrogate generation = fake values to re-run tests? won't teams complain it's not the real input?
Asha: yes it's not the raw input. goal is safe, deterministic surrogates so retries exercise the same code paths. e.g., same string lengths, email format preserved, deterministic mapping from field-id -> surrogate.
Leah: How do we prevent reverse engineering? HMAC with tenant KMS is irreversible as long as key is kept secret. good.
Ben: What about GDPR deletion? tenants can ask to delete their data; how do we locate every occurrence of a value if it's HMACed?
Asha: logs will have key-version metadata. deletion flow: rotate tenant key, scrub logs per retention+legal flags, and mark deleted occurrences in metadata. we'll document limits in legal FAQ.
Ivy: Attachments and embeddings are a bigger risk. they can leak content in vector stores. plan: compute compact chunk fingerprints for attachments and hashed-span ids for embeddings; store only fingerprints and apply same join logic.
Rory: Sampling: even at 0.1% our joins will help much more. field ids should be small (32 hex) and add minimal index cost.
Leah: Console UX idea: show "redacted" plus a tiny gray id badge. have an action "Preview surrogate" that renders a watermark-stamped surrogate in a modal. default hidden.
Ben: Ops unredact: we need a strict breakglass. require ticket, 2 approvers (legal + sec), ephemeral decrypt key from KMS, and an immutable audit entry.
Asha: agreed. extend existing breakglass flow with TTL-limited decryption; log requester, approvers, key-id.
Ivy: Routing: add an opt-in debug route to a small pool with no sampling. header X-RI-Debug: debug-route. default is off. enforce per-tenant quota to avoid abuse.
Rory: Billing/Quota: debug pool should be charged or metered separately; otherwise folks will burn capacity. add a console toggle per-tenant with quota caps.
Leah: Collision risk? HMAC_SHA256 collisions negligible but we'll monitor for anomalies: same field-id appearing with conflicting field-type or different hashed prefixes. alert if seen.
Ben: Perf: computing HMAC per sensitive field may add CPU at ingress. we should prototype a middleware and benchmark. also ensure surrogate gen is extremely cheap.
Asha: I'll build a middleware prototype that: detects sensitive fields (schema + heuristics), applies HMAC with tenant key-version, emits telemetry, and optionally synthesizes surrogate for replay endpoints.
Ivy: For SDKs, provide a client middleware that can set X-RI-Debug and let devs opt-in to debug routing for local QA. default off. devex will write docs.
OpsBot: feature-flag created: "fieldline_sampling_join" on eng-platform.
Rory: Rollout suggestion: telemetry-only first (emit ids but no UI change) for 2 weeks, console canary next (3 weeks), debug routing + quotas (4 weeks), enterprise unredact with audited flow last (6 weeks).
Leah: Metrics to watch: number of support tickets referencing surrogates, rate of unredact requests, collision alerts, debug-pool usage and cost.
Ben: Also check false-positive joins that could create noisy correlations in analytics.
Asha: I'll include perf numbers and a cost estimate for the debug pool in the RFC/PR. opening RFC after prototype.
Ivy: tagging privacy for review @legal-team.
Asha: Thanks — PR incoming.
OpsBot: RFC ticket created: RFC-1753337777-fieldline (https://r.ticket/1753337777).
